02

A college runs on a hundred small tasks. Alpha holds them together.

Coordinators like Imran don't open one app to do one thing — they check a timetable, approve an application, log a complaint and confirm a meeting, often inside the same five minutes. The brief was to design a system that keeps pace with that rhythm, without ever feeling busy.

  • i

    Reduce the distance to routine tasks

    Batches, timetable, applications and complaints surfaced directly on the home screen — no digging through menus.

  • ii

    Give meetings a real workflow

    Requesting, scheduling and tracking meetings needed the structure of a proper booking tool, not a form buried in settings.

  • iii

    Make status legible at a glance

    Pending, in-progress, resolved, approved, rejected — every list uses the same colour logic so status never needs a second look.

  • iv

    Carry one identity throughout

    The red-on-white mark from the login screen extends into every header, pill and state — the app never stops feeling like Alpha.

Process

Four stages, each closing the gap between how a coordinator actually works and how the old flow made them work.

01

Discover

Shadowed a coordinator's day to map every task and bottleneck.

02

Structure

Rebuilt navigation around three simple anchors.

03

Design

Extended the Alpha mark into a full design system.

04

Refine

Stress-tested with dense, real-world data.

05

Designed at a teacher's desk, not a design desk.

Every screen was checked against one question: does this still make sense with a class waiting outside the door? Alpha is built to be read in five seconds between periods, not studied at a laptop.

Getting in

Splash · Login

First impressions carry the identity. The splash sequence introduces the wordmark on the brand red before handing off to a login built around a single clear action.

Splash — brand entry

Full-bleed red, logo-led

Splash — mark reveal

Two-tone wordmark transition

Splash — light variant

Outline mark on tinted grey

Login

One card, one action, no clutter

Sign-in stays legible even at a glance — the kind of screen a teacher checks between periods, not in a quiet office.

07
Home

The home screen answers "what's next" before it's asked.

Identity, today's date and the newest announcement sit above the fold — then the six menus a coordinator opens most, arranged as a grid instead of a list, so nothing is more than one glance away.

  • Profile card confirms who's logged in and their live status
  • Latest announcement is never buried in a feed
  • Bottom nav keeps Meetings one tap away at all times
08

Running the academics

Batches · Timetable · Applications

The heaviest data in the app — class lists, weekly schedules, applications — needed structure before style. Cards group what belongs together; colour is reserved for status only.

Batches

Campus & headcount at a glance

Batch details

Tutors, subjects, task menu

Timetable

Colour-coded day rail with recess built in

Applications

Approved / pending / rejected, reasoned

09
Complaints

A complaint list that respects the person reading it.

Pending, in-progress and resolved live in their own tabs with a live count, so a coordinator opens the screen already knowing the size of the queue — before reading a single line.

  • Search-first layout for fast lookup by keyword
  • Tab counts double as a workload indicator
  • Floating action makes logging a new complaint a single tap
10

Meetings, treated like a real booking

Request · Track

Meetings moved from a buried form to a proper flow: request with full context, then track it through scheduled, done or cancelled — a status a coordinator actually needs to report on.

Request meeting

Mode, type and participants in one form

Meetings list

Pending, done and cancelled, filterable

11
Announcements

From a scannable feed to the full, formal notice.

The list stays visual and brief — image, date, one line. Opening a card hands over the complete, correctly formatted notice, attachments included, so nothing important is ever summarised away.

Profile & Settings

Official, basic and personal information — kept visibly separate.

Employee ID and department sit apart from CNIC and bank details, so sensitive information is never one careless scroll away from the wrong eyes. "More" keeps account actions just as unambiguous.

Pulled directly from the shipped screens — the palette was already there, it just needed rules.

Alpha Red#E7191F

60·30·10Colour ratio rule
Alpha Red45%
Deep Maroon25%
Garnet12%
Paper12%
Ink6%

Red carries identity and action, maroon and garnet hold depth and surfaces, paper and ink stay reserved for content — so colour always tells you what to look at first.

Grid & spacing

A 4-column mobile grid with an 20px outer margin and 12px gutter keeps every card, list and form aligned to the same rhythm, screen after screen.
